books.title: Lecture 1: Pelvic skeleton, joints and organization of pelvic viscera
books.author: Prof. Dr. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany
books.subject: Anatomy
books.summary: Anatomy lecture on the bony pelvis, its joints and ligaments, inlet/outlet, and the arrangement of pelvic viscera and peritoneal pouches in males and females.

chunks.title: Overview: pelvic skeleton and hip bone
chunks.summary: Title slide (Prof. Abdelghany Hassan Abdelghany, Alexandria University). The pelvis is formed by two hip bones plus the sacrum posteriorly. Each hip bone is formed of three bones (ilium, ischium, pubis) that join at the acetabulum.

chunks.title: Iliac bone (ilium)
chunks.summary: Upper part of the hip bone. Iliac crest ends at the anterior superior and posterior superior iliac spines; anterior inferior and posterior inferior iliac spines lie below them. Pelvic (inner) surface with the iliac fossa; gluteal (outer) surface giving origin to gluteal muscles; auricular surface articulating with the sacrum; iliac tuberosity behind it.

chunks.title: Pubic bone and ischial bone
chunks.summary: Pubic bone (anterior part of hip bone): body articulating at the symphysis pubis with pubic tubercle and pubic crest (medial to tubercle); superior pubic ramus with pectineal line and pectineal surface; inferior pubic ramus joining the ischial ramus to form the ischiopubic ramus. Ischial bone (lower part): ramus, ischiopubic ramus (pubic arch is formed by the ischiopubic rami of both sides), ischial tuberosity, ischial spine separating greater sciatic notch (above) from lesser sciatic notch (below).

chunks.title: Sacrum: shape and surfaces
chunks.summary: Triangular bone forming the posterior bone of the pelvic skeleton; apex below, base above; formed of 5 fused sacral vertebrae; base has the sacral promontory and an ala on each side; 4 surfaces. Anterior surface: concave, 4 pairs of anterior sacral foramina, 4 transverse ridges (lines of fusion), origin of piriformis. Lateral surface: auricular surface in front and sacral tuberosity behind (auricular surface forms the sacroiliac joint). Posterior surface: convex, median sacral crest, 4 pairs of posterior sacral foramina, sacral hiatus, upper opening of the canal; sacral cornua articulate with coccygeal cornua.

chunks.title: Sacral canal, sacral hiatus and coccyx
chunks.summary: Sacral canal is the lower part of the vertebral canal; upper opening on the dorsum of the first sacral piece, lower opening is the sacral hiatus. Contents: dura mater and arachnoid, lateral sacral arteries, 5 pairs of sacral nerves, 1 pair of coccygeal nerves, filum terminale (lower extension of pia mater). Structures exiting the sacral hiatus: 5th sacral nerves, coccygeal nerves, filum terminale. Coccyx: 2-4 fused coccygeal vertebrae.

chunks.title: Pelvic joints and ligaments
chunks.summary: Symphysis pubis: joint between the bodies of the pubic bones with an intervening disc; a secondary cartilaginous joint. Sacroiliac joint has 2 compartments: anterior part between the auricular surfaces (synovial plane joint, sliding movements) and posterior part between the tuberosities (fibrous joint, syndesmosis, limited mobility); ligaments: anterior, interosseous and posterior sacroiliac. Sacrotuberous ligament (sacrum and coccyx to ischial tuberosity) and sacrospinous ligament (to ischial spine) convert the greater and lesser sciatic notches into foramina.

chunks.title: Pelvic inlet, outlet, divisions and position
chunks.summary: Pelvic inlet: bounded by symphysis pubis, pubic crest, pubic tubercle, pectineal line, arcuate line and ala of sacrum on each side, and the sacral promontory posteriorly. Pelvic outlet: inferior surface of symphysis pubis, pubic arch, ischial tuberosities, sacrotuberous ligaments and tip of coccyx. Greater (false) pelvis lies above the inlet and contains abdominal viscera; lesser (true) pelvis lies between inlet and outlet and contains pelvic viscera and perineum. Anatomical position: pubic tubercles and anterior superior iliac spines lie in the same vertical plane.

chunks.title: Pelvic viscera and peritoneal reflections (male and female)
chunks.summary: Males: bladder most anterior with urethra from its lower end, prostate below the bladder, rectum most posterior; peritoneum passes from the anterior abdominal wall to the bladder's upper surface and upper posterior surface, then onto the rectum forming the rectovesical pouch. Females: bladder anterior, uterus above the bladder with the cervix behind it, vagina behind the bladder, rectum posterior, uterine tube on each side opening into the uterus and ending at the ovary; peritoneum passes from the abdominal wall to the bladder then the lower uterus forming the uterovesical pouch, then covers the uterus and posterior vagina and reflects onto the rectum forming the rectovaginal (rectouterine) pouch of Douglas.

chunks.title: Self-test: true/false and MCQ with answers
chunks.summary: End-of-lecture questions with answers. True/false: lesser pelvis lies above the pelvic inlet (False); rectovesical pouch is a peritoneal pouch in females (False); 4th and 5th pairs of sacral nerves exit the sacral hiatus (False); symphysis pubis is a secondary cartilaginous joint (True). MCQ: type of the anterior part of the sacroiliac joint (synovial plane). Final slide is a thank-you slide.
